title: Implicit Drifting Policy: One-Step Action Generation via Conditional Expert Geometry
claim: Prior methods build unstable targets from sparse, evolving samples; ours derives a stable local geometry directly from similar expert data.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, left-to-right, contrasting scatter plots with shared legend below
description: Two side-by-side 2D scatter diagrams with a shared legend underneath. Panel (a), 'Explicit Drifting', shows a large dashed purple ellipse of expert action points and an overlapping dashed blue ellipse of generated samples. At their intersection a white query point has a black arrow V, a dashed purple arrow V+ and a blue arrow V-, each in a labeled box. A blue 'Extra samples' label sits below. Panel (b), 'Implicit Drifting', has the same purple expert cloud, but a solid teal ellipse encloses a dense cluster of teal expert-neighbor points. A black arrow points from a query point into this cluster. A teal 'Conditional Expert Geometry' label sits at the lower right. The legend lists purple expert actions, blue generated samples and teal expert neighbors. The eye goes first to the colored ellipses and the arrows.
caption: (a) Explicit Drifting constructs targets by estimating a drifting field between expert actions (purple) and policy predictions (blue). Relying on the evolving policy state and mini-batch sampling makes this target sensitive and unstable. (b) Implicit Drifting Policy (Ours) directly extracts a Conditional Expert Geometry (green) from expert actions under similar observations.
abstract: Generative action policies based on diffusion or flow matching excel in behavior cloning, yet their iterative sampling is prohibitive for high-frequency robot control. While recent one-step formulations alleviate this latency, they inevitably discard the intermediate trajectory evolution that provides crucial action correction. Directly recovering this mechanism by explicitly estimating a training-time drifting field is mathematically ill-posed due to extreme conditional demonstration sparsity. We introduce Implicit Drifting Policy (IDP), a one-step imitation learning framework that brings the training-time correction of Drifting into policy learning without explicit vector field estimation. IDP extracts a conditional expert geometry from the local variation of observation-similar expert actions, and compares it against a global reference geometry to isolate condition-specific constraints. This local geometric structure adaptively weights a scalar potential objective. Combined with an expert-proximal terminal evaluation, IDP directly enforces manifold constraints on the one-step generator during training. Extensive evaluations across 2D, 3D, and real-world manipulation tasks show IDP effectively maintains adherence to valid action manifolds, improving upon explicit drifting methods and achieving competitive performance with strong one-step baselines.
